name: Tehran
why: Iran's capital and biggest city. The government and the Supreme Leader's office are here.

name: Isfahan
why: Big city in central Iran. A nuclear technology centre and uranium plant sit just outside it. The IAEA says it does not know the plant's status.

name: Tabriz
why: Biggest city in Iran's northwest, close to Turkey, Armenia and Azerbaijan.

name: Mashhad
why: Iran's second biggest city, in the far northeast near Turkmenistan and Afghanistan. A major religious centre.

name: Shiraz
why: Big city in the south. It has a major air base and sits on the road to the Gulf coast.

name: Qom
why: Religious city south of Tehran. The Fordow nuclear site is dug into a mountain nearby.

name: Bandar Abbas
why: Iran's main port and navy base, right on the Strait of Hormuz.

name: Bushehr nuclear power plant
why: Iran's only working nuclear power station, on the Persian Gulf coast. Built with Russian help.

name: Natanz
why: Iran's main uranium enrichment site, partly underground. Enrichment is the step that can lead to bomb fuel.

name: Fordow
why: Uranium enrichment site built deep inside a mountain near Qom. It was bombed in June 2025, and the IAEA has had no access since.

name: Arak reactor
why: Heavy water reactor site near Arak. This kind of reactor can make plutonium, another possible bomb fuel.

name: Parchin
why: Military complex southeast of Tehran, long linked to missile and explosives work.

name: Kharg Island
why: Small island in the Persian Gulf. Most of Iran's crude oil exports are loaded onto tankers here.
country_note: the island is too small to appear on the 1:50m country shapes

name: Chabahar
why: Iran's only ocean port, on the Gulf of Oman outside the Strait of Hormuz. India has invested in it.

name: Qeshm Island
why: Iran's biggest island, lying along the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian forces are based on it.

name: Strait of Hormuz
why: Narrow passage between Iran and Oman. A large share of the world's oil and gas normally passes through it.
country_note: a sea passage between two countries

name: Persian Gulf
why: The sea between Iran and the Arab Gulf states. Much of the world's oil is loaded onto tankers here.

name: Gulf of Oman
why: The sea just outside the Strait of Hormuz, leading to the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean.

name: Caspian Sea
why: The world's largest lake, north of Iran. Iran shares it with Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan.

name: Red Sea
why: Sea between Africa and Arabia. Ships use it to reach the Suez Canal, the short route between Asia and Europe.

name: Arabian Sea
why: Part of the Indian Ocean south of Iran and Pakistan. US Navy carriers often operate here.

name: Bab al-Mandab
why: Narrow passage at the south end of the Red Sea, next to Yemen. Ships heading for the Suez Canal must pass it.
country_note: a sea passage between two countries

name: Suez Canal
why: Man-made canal in Egypt that links the Red Sea and the Mediterranean, the short sea route between Asia and Europe.

name: Mediterranean Sea
why: The sea between Europe, North Africa and the Middle East.

name: Black Sea
why: Sea shared by Ukraine, Russia, Turkey and others. Ukraine exports grain across it.

name: Al Udeid Air Base
why: The biggest US air base in the Middle East and the forward headquarters of US Central Command.

name: US Fifth Fleet base
why: Home of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, which patrols the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea and the Arabian Sea.
ref_note: Only OpenStreetMap has a coordinate for this place, so it has one reference.

name: Al Asad Air Base
why: Large air base in western Iraq that hosted US troops for years. Iraq took full control in January 2026, and the US-led coalition ended its mission in Iraq on 30 September.

name: Al Dhafra Air Base
why: Air base near Abu Dhabi used by US aircraft, across the Gulf from Iran.
osm: Al Dhafra Air Base, United Arab Emirates

name: Prince Sultan Air Base
why: Saudi air base south of Riyadh that hosts US aircraft and air defences.
osm: Prince Sultan Air Base, Saudi Arabia

name: Camp Arifjan
why: US Army base in Kuwait, a supply hub for US forces in the region.

name: Diego Garcia
why: Remote island base in the Indian Ocean used by US long-range bombers.
country_note: a remote island not drawn on the country shapes

name: Jerusalem
why: Seat of Israel's government. Its status is disputed, and Palestinians want East Jerusalem as their capital.

name: Tel Aviv
why: Israel's business centre and home of its military headquarters. Most foreign embassies are here.

name: Gaza City
why: Biggest city in the Gaza Strip. A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas was announced in October 2025, but Israeli strikes continue.

name: Rafah
why: City at the south end of Gaza, on the border with Egypt.
ref_note: OpenStreetMap search returned nothing for this name; Wikipedia is the one reference.

name: Beirut
why: Lebanon's capital. Hezbollah, an armed group and party backed by Iran, is strong in its southern suburbs.

name: Bekaa Valley
why: Eastern Lebanon, along the Syrian border. A Hezbollah stronghold and supply route.

name: Damascus
why: Syria's capital. A new government took over after President Assad fell in December 2024.

name: Baghdad
why: Iraq's capital. Iraq's government balances between the US and Iran, and Iran-backed militias are strong here.

name: Jurf al-Sakhar
why: Town south of Baghdad controlled by Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militia.

name: Sanaa
why: Yemen's capital, held by the Houthis, an armed movement backed by Iran.

name: Riyadh
why: Capital of Saudi Arabia, the biggest Arab oil exporter and Iran's main rival across the Gulf.

name: Yanbu
why: Saudi oil port on the Red Sea. It lets Saudi Arabia export oil without using the Strait of Hormuz.

name: Doha
why: Capital of Qatar, a small gas-rich state that often carries messages between the US and Iran.

name: Manama
why: Capital of Bahrain, a small island state that hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.

name: Abu Dhabi
why: Capital of the United Arab Emirates, a rich Gulf state across the water from Iran.

name: Kuwait City
why: Capital of Kuwait, a small oil state at the top of the Persian Gulf between Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

name: Muscat
why: Capital of Oman, which shares the Strait of Hormuz with Iran and has often hosted quiet US and Iran talks.

name: Islamabad
why: Capital of Pakistan, Iran's eastern neighbour and a nuclear-armed state.

name: Kabul
why: Capital of Afghanistan, ruled by the Taliban since 2021.

name: Ankara
why: Capital of Turkey, a NATO member that borders Iran, Iraq and Syria.

name: Cairo
why: Capital of Egypt, which borders Gaza and runs the Suez Canal.

name: Washington, D.C.
why: Capital of the United States. Arrows from here mean a decision or action by the US government.

name: Corpus Christi
why: Oil port on the Texas coast.

name: Caracas
why: Capital of Venezuela, which has the world's largest known oil reserves.

name: Moscow
why: Capital of Russia.

name: Kyiv
why: Capital of Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022.

name: Crimean Bridge
why: Bridge over the Kerch Strait that links Russia to Crimea, the Ukrainian peninsula Russia seized in 2014.
ref_note: Only OpenStreetMap has a coordinate for this place, so it has one reference.
country_note: a bridge over water between Russia and occupied Crimea

name: Vienna
why: Capital of Austria and home of the IAEA, the UN agency that inspects nuclear sites.

name: London
why: Capital of the United Kingdom.

name: Beijing
why: Capital of China. Arrows from here mean a decision or action by China's government.

name: Hong Kong
why: A special administrative region of China on its south coast and a major hub for finance and trade.

name: Taipei
why: Capital of Taiwan, a self-governed island that China claims as its own territory.

name: Taiwan Strait
why: The sea between China and Taiwan, about 130 to 180 km wide, and a busy shipping route.

name: Tokyo
why: Capital of Japan, a US ally.

name: Seoul
why: Capital of South Korea, a US ally, only about 50 km from the North Korean border.

name: Pyongyang
why: Capital of North Korea, which has nuclear weapons and tests missiles often.

name: Sea of Japan (East Sea)
why: The sea between Japan and the Korean peninsula. Korea calls it the East Sea. North Korean test missiles often land here.

name: Manila
why: Capital of the Philippines, a US treaty ally.

name: Scarborough Shoal
why: Ring of reefs in the South China Sea claimed by both China and the Philippines. China has controlled it since 2012.
country_note: a disputed reef in open sea

name: South China Sea
why: Sea between China, Vietnam, the Philippines and Malaysia. China claims most of it, and about a third of world shipping crosses it.

name: Jakarta
why: Capital of Indonesia.

name: New Delhi
why: Capital of India.

name: Khartoum
why: Sudan's capital, where the civil war began in April 2023.

name: Port Sudan
why: Red Sea port that became the base of Sudan's army-led government during the war.

name: El Obeid
why: Main city of Sudan's Kordofan region and an army stronghold.

name: Al-Khuway
why: Town in West Kordofan on the road towards Darfur.
ref_note: Only OpenStreetMap has a coordinate for this place, so it has one reference.

name: El Fasher
why: Main city of North Darfur in western Sudan.

name: Addis Ababa
why: Capital of Ethiopia, Africa's second most populous country.

name: Mekelle
why: Capital of Ethiopia's northern Tigray region. A TPLF-led alliance briefly held it until 3 October 2026; government-allied forces then took it.

name: Asmara
why: Capital of Eritrea, Ethiopia's northern neighbour on the Red Sea.

name: Zalambessa
why: Ethiopian town right on the border with Eritrea.

name: Bamako
why: Capital of Mali, ruled by the army since coups in 2020 and 2021.

name: Kidal
why: Desert town in northern Mali, long a base of Tuareg rebels. Mali's army says it retook it on 6 October 2026.

name: Rudnik nad Sanem
why: Town in southeast Poland near where Russian missiles fell on 20 November 2026.

name: Berlin
why: Capital of Germany.
